what_this_is: THE RULES AS DATA, not code. The direction's non-foreclosure resolution requires evaluator DEFINITIONS to be portable — 'they can be pointed at a different system without being rewritten' — so the classes and thresholds live here and the code is a thin reader. This is the single thing that keeps the gate from foreclosing a non-Hermes runtime. ADR-001 §6-§7.
why_the_agent_must_route_through_this: The gate cannot intercept a reply — there is no pre-send hook, and the send is deliberately not a tool call. So it refuses at the points the agent chooses to route through, and measures coverage rather than claiming to catch everything. ADR-001 §1 and §4.
methods_note: Straight from the direction's own definition of a discoverable question: 'search, measurement, reading the repo, probing the record, running the code'. An attempt that names none of these is not an attempt.
seat_note: The Owner's own rule: on every escalation, ask which seat is answering. An escalation that does not name one cannot be answered in the right capacity.

refusal_style.rule: A refusal must name what is missing and what would satisfy it. 'Invalid' teaches nothing, so a refusal that only says invalid is itself a defect — the same principle as the corpus gate naming the field it rejected.

gateable_paths.note: Three paths reach the Owner and two are gateable. `clarify` is blocked by a pre_tool_call hook unless an escalation was accepted this turn. The third — a question typed into an ordinary reply — is not gateable in this host, and that is the declared gap (ADR-001 §4).
